hook.text: Delivery trucks account for 30% of city traffic but make up most of the congestion during business hours.

buildup.text: Urban deliveries compete for road space with commuters, buses, bikes, and pedestrians.

discovery.text: Double-parking, narrow streets, and delivery time restrictions make city logistics slow and expensive.

twist.text: More e-commerce means more vans. Cities that don't plan for delivery traffic will choke on it.

climax.text: Cities like London and Paris are creating dedicated delivery zones and off-peak delivery programs.

punchline.text: Every online order puts another van on a crowded street.

quiz.question: What share of city traffic do delivery trucks represent?
